_doc: Nhạn Trận Môn lineage (rules-proposals R5), a no-lean war-formation school (R3): leans Metal, Earth -> none. Its seat (367) fails Metal/Earth and no place in its ground fits Metal (Metal 9-16 % everywhere on the plain). Outer gate: mountain-bone-body-art (existing body, Yellow). Inner gate and above: wild-geese-formation-canon (proposal, Profound, element-free formation). Secret arts: spring-levy-drum (inner gate), walking-out-of-the-grey (elders and the head; the founders'). The body art is also the outer method. Unpriced.

secret.note: the founders' art; taught only to the head and the elders

lineage.tree_route_note: Earth Root, Earthen Gate, Five Peaks: block and health for a file that does not break. The lineage has no element; priced from Earth, the start of most of its A/B members (25; Water 55).

techniques.name: Wild Geese Formation Canon (Nhạn Trận Kinh)
techniques.concept: A method for a file, not for one person. Each disciple learns to pass qi down the line the way geese trade the lead in a long flight: the one at the point takes the wind, and when the point tires it falls back and the next takes it. The canon cultivates no element. It trains the meridians to give and take a share of a neighbour's strain, so a file of five fights as one body with five pairs of hands. Singly, a disciple of the gate is ordinary. In file they are very hard to break, and they get stronger the longer the line holds.

arts.concept: A formation stance: while the file holds, you take 18 % less damage, regain 15 % of each damaging blow taken (once a pulse, sharing strain down the file), and gain a 3 % health stance ward every 3 s. This is the stance Cảnh Trường Thiên carried into Lạc Hà's Autumn Water and the Long Sky.
For 4 s you take 30 % less damage; then the stance ends and clears one curse from you.

techniques.lore: Written down by the founder Thạch Liệt Hàng from nine years of drill under Lạc Hà's Cảnh Trường Thiên (806-815, V096), and named for Nhạn Thanh Thành, where the geese cross the walls in formation (C092).

techniques.name: Drum of the Spring Levy (Xuân Điểm Cổ Pháp)
techniques.concept: The drum the gate beats when it drills the plain's mortal levies on the shore of Lạc Nhạn Hồ each spring. The drummer's qi goes into the beat, and the beat goes into the feet of everyone who hears it in time: a line of farmers keeps its spacing under arrows, and a file of disciples moves at one pace. In a fight the drum sets the file's rhythm and closes gaps when someone falls.

arts.concept: When you are first Wounded, for 5 s you gain attack speed (your companions half) and take 10 % less damage.

techniques.lore: The levy drum was first beaten in 807. Lạc Hà's Thảo Đường Thành and Nhạn Thanh Thành pay the gate for every spring it drills their farmers.

techniques.name: Walking Out of the Grey (Xuất Hôi Đoạn Hậu Pháp)
techniques.concept: The founders' art, made on one night. On Chiết Kích Nguyên in 803 Thạch Liệt Hàng's file of forty was inside the grey when it rose. They held their line, breathed through one wet cloth passed down the file, one breath each, and walked out backwards with the rear guard facing the halberds. The art teaches that: a file that shares its breath shares its poison, and a shared poison is a halved poison. In a fight it spreads curses, poisons and stacks laid on one member across the whole file, so no one carries enough to fall, and it lets the file give ground without breaking.

arts.new: One Breath Down the File (Nhất Tức Truyền Hàng)
arts.concept: Breathes through the wet cloth for 8 s: clears 2 debuff stacks and 1 curse at once, grants +30 % status resistance for 8 s, and sheds 1 debuff stack each second as the file shares the poison.

arts.new: The Rear Guard Faces Back (Hậu Vệ Hồi Thân)
arts.concept: For 3 s you gain evasion and a ward, and you strike the foe once (a free hit).

techniques.lore: Never written down until Thạch's death in 1040. It is taught only to the head and the elders. Mục Tân Vũ, the point of the first file, has not been taught it, and she is learning it anyway from Thạch's notes.
